hook.text: High-yield seeds need reliable water. Rainfed farmers—the majority worldwide—got far less benefit.

buildup.text: India's Green Revolution concentrated in Punjab and Haryana—regions with extensive canal and well irrigation.

discovery.text: Dry-land farmers in central and eastern India saw little yield improvement. The revolution passed them by.

twist.text: To extend benefits, governments subsidized tube wells. Groundwater pumping soared—and aquifers began declining.

climax.text: The Green Revolution's water demand created today's groundwater crisis in India, Pakistan, and China.

punchline.text: High yields need water. The bill arrives a generation later.

quiz.question: Why did rainfed farmers benefit less from the Green Revolution?
options: High-yield varieties required reliable irrigation they didn't have
